To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the regulation of the rat interstittial collagenase gene is a complex process that requires the activation of multiple cis‐elements.

(1) IL‐1β regulates rat interstitial collagenases (rICL) promoter activity through multiple cis‐acting elements, (2) the proximal TRE is necessary for basal and IL‐1β–stimulated rICL promoter activity, (3) the nuclear binding protein c‐Jun is a component of IL‐1β‐induced TRE binding activity, (4) the Ras signaling pathway is involved in the regulation of rICL promoter function, and (5

(i) the promoter of the rat intercollagenase gene is regulated in a stage‐specific manner by multiple cis‐acting elements; (ii) IL‐1β regulates the promoter through a TRE and c‐Jun binding protein; (iii) Ras‐dependent signaling is involved in the regulation of the rat intercolagenase gene; and (iv) the regulation of the intercolagenase promoter is susceptible to inhibition of Ras‐signaling.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regulation of interstitial collagenase in cartilage cells is complex.

the regulation of the rat interstellar collagenase promoter is a complex process that involves both proximal and distant regulatory sites and multiple signaling pathways that may vary with the stage of chonodrocyte differentiation.
the activation of c‐Jun, the binding to TRE, and Ras‐dependent signaling are important for the regulation of rat collagenase expression in growth plate chondoctyes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the regulation of the rat intercollagenase gene is a combinatoral process, and multiple cis‐regulatory sites may interact to produce different effects dependent on stage of chondrocye differentiation.

the regulation of collagenase gene expression involves a combinatorial effect of multiple cis‐acting elements, which may interact to exert differential effects dependent on the state of chondroycyte differentiation.

the regulation of the rat interstital collagenase promoter by interleukin (1L‐1)β and c‐Jun is Ras‐dependent and that this regulation is more effective in proliferating chondrocyts than in hypertrophic cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activation of transcription factors that bind TREs may be a common feature in the regulation of IL‐1β–responsive genes in growth plate chondoctyes.

the regulation of collagenase gene expression involves multiple signaling pathways, and that the relative importance of each pathway may be dependent on the stage or type of chondro‐ or osteo‐cyte differentiation.
